# Space Atrapos - Tutorial

# lessons | Lessons
First steps, one topic at a time: what to do, in the order you'll need it. The [Pilot's guide](doc:start) has every detail; the Controls book lists every key.

## t-getting-started | Getting Started
[b]Welcome, pilot.[/b]

You are an automaton built by Ephestos, flying a light ship in [b]New Hellas[/b] - star systems in 3D you cross on the Hyperion drive, planets you fly down to and walk, stations you land on by hand, the old monsters in the void.

[b]Your first steps[/b]
1. Move the mouse off the middle of the screen: the ship turns. [b]W[/b] opens the throttle.
2. Press [b]T[/b] with a planet near the middle of your view to target it, then [b]J[/b]: the Hyperion drive takes you there.
3. Come down low and slow over level ground and press [b]L[/b] to land. [b]E[/b] stands you up; walk down the ramp at the back of your ship.
4. Back aboard ([b]E[/b] at the foot of the ramp, [b]E[/b] by the seat), take off with [b]L[/b]. Near a station, [b]L[/b] asks for a landing pad.
5. Press [b]Tab[/b] any time to open the Automaton.

## t-flying | Flying
The mouse is a [b]virtual stick[/b]: the further from the middle (the sights' inner ring), the faster the ship pitches and turns. [b]C[/b] or the middle button centres it.

• [b]W / S[/b] set the throttle - it stays where you leave it; [b]X[/b] stops.
• [b]A / D[/b] roll; [b]Shift[/b] boosts.
• [b]R / F[/b] fire the thrusters up and down, [b]Q / E[/b] sideways - for landing on pads.
• The [b]wheel[/b] moves the camera in and out; hold the [b]right button[/b] to look round.

The [b]compass bar[/b] at the top gives your heading; in the [b]sights[/b], VEL on the left is your speed and ALT on the right your height over the nearest world. Beside your health gauge, the [b]readout[/b]: the drive, the throttle - and near a planet your latitude and longitude.

## t-hyperion | The Hyperion drive
[b]J[/b] charges it (two seconds), then the ship races across the system at up to 250 km/s.

• Target something first ([b]T[/b]): the drive turns you to it - leave the mouse alone - engages once you're lined up, steers round what's in the way, and drops you out about 1.5 km from it.
• [b]Gravity wells[/b] slow it: near a planet, moon or the star the drive can't go as fast (the readout names the well).
• Flying too close to anything, or being shot, drops you out. Any planet of a system is seconds to a minute away.

## t-landing | Landing and walking
Planets are whole worlds of real ground - what you see from orbit is what you land on.

1. Come within 160 m of the ground, slower than 80 m/s, over dry, level ground clear of trees and boulders - [b]L[/b] lands (the readout says why not when it can't).
2. [b]E[/b] stands you up from the seat. Walk through your ship - its terminals open the Automaton's pages - and down the ramp at the back.
3. [b]W A S D[/b] walk, [b]Shift[/b] runs, [b]Space[/b] jumps, the [b]left button[/b] fires your rifle.
4. Back up the ramp and [b]E[/b] by the seat to fly again.

[b]Build[/b] a home of your own: the terrain digger ([b]3[/b]) cuts building stone loose as it digs, and the trees it fells give timber. Take the builder ([b]5[/b]) - a click lays a foundation where its preview shows green, then walls on its edges, a door, a ceiling, a roof ([b]N[/b] picks the piece, [b]K[/b] turns it, [b]O[/b] demolishes).

Watch out for [b]predators[/b] and [b]pirate camps[/b] (a red light on a mast). The inhabited worlds have [b]towns[/b] - their palaces, houses, people - each with a landing field beside it: from orbit, [b]T[/b] targets a town.

## t-combat | Combat
The [b]left button[/b] fires your ship's weapons - the ones fitted on its hardpoints; [b]1-9[/b] pick one on the toolbar. With a ship targeted ([b]T[/b]), a ring shows where to aim to hit it.

• [b]Shields[/b] (the blue ring) soak hits and come back after a few seconds; the [b]hull[/b] (red) doesn't.
• [b]Pirate raiders[/b] come for you now and then - more in lawless systems. Each one destroyed pays a bounty.
• Keep away from the [b]star[/b]: its heat burns your shields, then your hull.

## t-monsters | The old monsters
Every system has its [b]unknown bio-signatures[/b] - markers on your screen with how dangerous they are. Each is a monster's lair: the Void Leviathan, Cetus, Charybdis, Skylla, the Hydra, Cerberus, the Chimera, Echidna or the Minotaur.

• Come near and it comes for you. When its glow gathers, orbs are coming: a ring round you with a gap in the middle (hold still), fans, spirals, blooms.
• Keep moving, keep firing - hit it anywhere along its body. Its shields come back if you let up.
• Slain, it pays a bounty - bigger for the harder ones.

## t-stations | Docking at a station
Stations are kilometres across, with numbered landing pads at the ends of their arms.

1. Near a station, press [b]L[/b]: you're given a pad - it lights up and is marked on your screen.
2. Fly over it, slow down, and come down on the thrusters ([b]F[/b] down, [b]Q / E[/b] sideways). The landing display shows the pad from above - steer its square under your ship - your height, the level bubble and your speed.
3. Touch down level and slower than 12 m/s: the pad's lift takes you into the [b]hangar[/b].
4. Get up, walk down the ramp: the terminals along the back wall ([b]E[/b]) are the station's [b]Market[/b], [b]Workshop[/b], [b]Outfitting[/b], [b]Shipyard[/b], [b]Missions[/b] and more.
5. Back aboard, [b]L[/b] undocks: up the lift and off.

## t-trading | Trading
Every station has a live [b]Market[/b]. Stations [b]produce[/b] some goods and [b]need[/b] others; prices follow supply - cheap where goods are made, dear where they're scarce.


Production chains link the stations: a station short of its inputs (shown in red) slows down - and pays more for them. System states and wars shift demand too (weapons, fuel and medicine sell high in wartime).

[b]NPC traders[/b] fly these routes, each with their own cargo and drachmas - and so can you. Your hold size depends on your ship and its cargo racks.

[b]Pirate raiders[/b] prey on the traders - and on you. Each one destroyed pays a bounty.

## t-empires-reputation | Empires & Reputation
You answer to no empire. Your [b]reputation[/b] with each of them - and with the [b]Independents[/b] - is all that counts, from [b]Hostile[/b] through Unfriendly, Neutral, Cordial and Friendly to [b]Allied[/b] (the station's [b]Reputation[/b] tab shows it).


- It [b]rises[/b] with missions at their stations, trading there (every 10,000 dr bought or sold: +1 - reputation grows slowly) and hunting Sea Peoples raiders in their space.
- It [b]falls[/b] when you attack their ships: a little for the first shot at one, more for each one destroyed. It takes several to make an enemy - and a bad name fades back toward Neutral with time.
- [b]Hostile[/b]: their warships attack you and their stations refuse you. Better standing brings better missions (Trusted, Honoured), better prices and bigger bounties.

Most stations in a system belong to the empire holding it. The rest are [b]independent[/b] free ports (neutral with everyone, out of every war), an ally's [b]outpost[/b] (opened with the owner's leave) or a [b]forward base[/b] of an empire at war with the owner, wearing the system down to take it. When a system falls, its stations change hands.

## t-ships-outfitting | Ships & Outfitting
The [b]Shipyard[/b] at each station sells its empire's designs - fighters, gunships, frigates, cruisers, dreadnoughts, freighters, mining barges and explorers. Your old ship is traded in.


Each ship has [b]hardpoints[/b] (weapons), [b]internal slots[/b] and [b]utility mounts[/b]. [b]Outfitting[/b] sells modules rated [b]E[/b] (cheap) to [b]A[/b] (best): shield generators, hull reinforcement, cargo racks, thrusters, shield cell banks, gimballed mounts and shield amplifiers - plus the weapons and active systems.

## t-missions | Missions
Each station's [b]Missions[/b] tab offers eight jobs. You can run up to [b]five at once[/b]; active missions are listed at the top right of the screen.


• [b]Pirate Sweep[/b] - destroy a number of enemies of any kind.
• [b]Hunt[/b] - destroy a specific ship class. Hunted classes show up more often while the mission is active. Big targets also pay a Data Core.
• [b]Courier[/b] - dock at another station to deliver a package.
• [b]Supply Run[/b] - buy trade goods at a market and deliver them to another station.
• [b]Salvage Request / Mining Contract[/b] - bring salvage or ore back to the issuing station and press Turn In.
• [b]Survey[/b] - fly to an uncharted point (marked on your map) to scan it.

Missions come in four tiers - [b]Routine, Trusted, Honoured, Hero[/b] - needing reputation 0, 10, 25 and 50 with the station's empire; the better ones pay more. Ones you aren't trusted with yet are [b]greyed out[/b]. Every mission you finish raises your reputation with that empire (more for the higher tiers). Kill, courier, supply and survey missions pay out automatically when completed. You can abandon a mission at any station.

## t-saving | Saving
Press [b]Esc[/b] for the menu.

• [b]Save[/b] stores the galaxy, your ship, drachmas, cargo, equipment, tech, missions and where you are.
• [b]Load[/b] restores a save (also from the title screen); [b]Continue[/b] on the title screen loads the latest.
• The game also saves by itself when you dock and when you come through a gate.
• [b]Exit to desktop[/b] closes the game.
